headline: Network & Cloud Engineer | Routing & Switching | AWS | Linux
summary: Electronics and Communications Engineering graduate with networking depth (CCNA curriculum and Huawei HCIA-Datacom course, studied) applied in the cloud: multi-AZ VPC design, private subnets behind NAT, default-deny security groups, a WireGuard VPN with per-team address ranges and a Squid proxy with per-team rules. Designed a two-floor building network in Cisco Packet Tracer using routers and switches.

bullets.text: Completed intensive hands-on training in Linux administration, networking, CI/CD, containerization, and cloud infrastructure, culminating in end-to-end DevOps projects (see Projects).
Applied DevOps best practices to production-tier projects, covering CI/CD, GitOps, containerization, and infrastructure automation.

bullets.label: Infrastructure & Access
bullets.text: Enterprise-style RHEL environment on EC2 (VPN gateway, control, identity, utility and per-team workstations) in private subnets behind a NAT gateway, built with modular Terraform; reachable only through a WireGuard VPN with per-team ranges, firewalld and default-deny security groups.

bullets.label: Identity & Team Policy
bullets.text: FreeIPA centralizes users, DNS, Kerberos, HBAC and sudo rules per team; the utility server runs a Squid proxy with per-team internet rules, NFS home directories, centralized logging and backups.
Designed the network for a two-floor building in Cisco Packet Tracer using routers, switches and end devices.

bullets.label: Platform & Security
bullets.text: Five Python/FastAPI banking microservices and an NGINX frontend on EKS, built for financial correctness (fencing tokens, row-lock ordering). Versioned Terraform modules deploy through GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD App-of-Apps, secured with default-deny NetworkPolicies, Istio mTLS, Gateway API and External Secrets Operator (IRSA).

Modular Terraform for a 3-tier AWS app (VPC, ALBs, Auto Scaling groups, RDS) with tier-isolated security groups, deployed through a Jenkins pipeline with a manual approval gate and monitored by CloudWatch alarms.
Three-tier app on Kubernetes secured with RBAC, default-deny NetworkPolicies, and Cilium FQDN-based egress rules, with Ingress and autoscaling.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Network Back Office Engineer role at Orbitel Networks. I combine network fundamentals from my engineering degree with hands-on cloud network design, and I want to bring that to a team that keeps networks running day to day.

Your core requirement is routing and switching. My base is the CCNA curriculum, which I studied but did not certify, and the Huawei HCIA-Datacom course, which I completed without taking the exam. I applied it by designing a two-floor building network in Cisco Packet Tracer with routers, switches and end devices. My OSPF, BGP and VLAN knowledge is at familiar level, and I have not run these protocols on live carrier equipment. On the operations side, I built an enterprise-style RHEL lab on AWS with private subnets behind a NAT gateway, default-deny security groups and a WireGuard VPN with per-team address ranges. Changes there were recorded in tickets, runbooks and 7 incident reports.

My degree and networking courses gave me the fundamentals; building VPNs, proxies and segmented VPCs on AWS showed me how much of reliability and security is decided in the network. A back office role keeps that network documented and working, which is the work I want to do. I would welcome a conversation, and my CV is attached.

email_body:
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Network Back Office Engineer role at Orbitel Networks.
My CV and cover letter are attached.
I bring CCNA and HCIA-Datacom coursework, a Cisco Packet Tracer design, and hands-on VPN, NAT and VPC work on AWS.
I would be glad to discuss the role.
why_this_role: This role builds on my Packet Tracer network design and my AWS work with NAT, WireGuard VPN and segmented VPCs, where I saw that reliability and security are largely decided in the network.
